title: Lena and the Letter
premise: Marguerite Underhill, host of the podcast 'Cold Ledger,' has spent a decade closing unsolvable cases—until a confession letter arrives for a murder that officially never happened, postmarked the day after the victim's funeral. The letter points to a coded ledger hidden inside the victim's family bakery, and as Marguerite decodes it, they realize the victim was documenting a decades-long identity swap within the town's founding family—and that the sender wants Marguerite, not justice. In the end, Marguerite exposes the living impostor on air, but chooses to keep one truth sealed: their own buried connection to the family, trading closure for belonging at last.
about_author: Rafael Quintana is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper reporter who spent years covering cold cases before turning to fiction. They live quietly near the coast, where they collect old ledgers and insist they've never taken a story they couldn't finish.

chapters.title: Postmarked Yesterday
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Days after covering the funeral of Edith Vale—a woman whose death certificate lists no cause—Marguerite receives a handwritten confession letter postmarked the morning after the burial. The letter names no victim, only a ledger 'kept where the bread rises.' The emotional beat is the crack in Marguerite's professional detachment: this case feels addressed to them personally.

chapters.title: The Case That Never Was
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Archive research reveals Edith Vale's death was never reported as suspicious, and the police file is one page long—deliberately thin. Marguerite interviews the funeral director, who mentions an unfamiliar woman in a green coat who left before the service ended. The beat: unease hardens into obsession.

chapters.title: Where the Bread Rises
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite visits Vale's shuttered bakery and finds the proofing cabinet lined with ledger pages written in a home cipher: dates, sums, and initials spanning forty years. The emotional beat is the thrill of the hunt colliding with the first hint that someone is watching from across the street.

chapters.title: Rules of the Host
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, with flashback. A flashback establishes Marguerite's iron rule—never take a case they can't close—and the personal wound behind it: a sister who vanished and was never found. Present-day Marguerite begins recording episodes, aware the podcast itself may be bait. The beat: vulnerability beneath control.

chapters.title: The Green Coat
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The woman in the green coat is identified as 'Lena Vale,' Edith's cousin—who officially died in 1987. Marguerite finds her living under another name two towns over. Lena denies sending the letter but confirms the cipher's first key. The beat: the dead walking, and Marguerite's certainties fraying.

chapters.title: First Sum, First Lie
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Decoded entries show payments to a 'R.U.' beginning in 1979—the year Edith's brother Rowan supposedly emigrated. Marguerite confronts the family's surviving matriarch, who answers questions with questions. The beat: the ledger is not accounting; it's blackmail, and Marguerite is holding the weapon.

chapters.title: Listener 44
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A recurring anonymous listener emails corrections to Marguerite's podcast episodes—corrections only the killer could make. The emails grow intimate, referencing Marguerite's vanished sister by a childhood nickname never made public. The beat: the hunter realizing they are also the quarry.

chapters.title: Rowan, Present Tense
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena reveals that Rowan never left: he assumed Edith's identity after her first 'death' in 1987, and Edith spent decades documenting the swap as insurance. Lena has been protecting the ledger—and Rowan knows. The beat: sympathy for the witness, dread for the target.

chapters.title: A Death Certificate, Twice Signed
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite obtains both death certificates—Edith's 1987 and the recent one—and finds the same coroner's signature, thirty-five years apart, aged identically. Someone inside the records office has been complicit for decades. The beat: the conspiracy has roots, not branches.

chapters.title: The Coroner's Drawer
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The retired coroner, found in assisted living, is lucid enough to confess he falsified the 1987 certificate under threat, and that the threat 'still sends flowers every May.' Marguerite realizes the flowers match entries in the ledger. The beat: pity curdling into fear—the sender is still active.

chapters.title: Interlude: What the Sister Knew
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, memory chapter. A dreamlike reconstruction of the night Marguerite's sister disappeared—same town, same year as Edith's first death, same bakery on the corner. Marguerite has been chasing this case longer than they admitted. The beat: the case and the wound become one.

chapters.title: Cipher of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Marguerite and Lena's alternating POV. Together they crack the ledger's final layer: it records not money but identities—names taken, names buried, names traded. The last page lists a name that has not yet been used. The beat: the ledger is a schedule, and the next swap is imminent.

chapters.title: The Empty Proofing Cabinet
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Returning to the bakery, Marguerite finds the ledger pages gone and the cabinet freshly scrubbed. A green coat hangs on the hook—Lena's. The beat: betrayal or sacrifice? Marguerite can no longer tell ally from accomplice.

chapters.title: Listener 44 Signs Off
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The anonymous listener sends a final email: a photograph of Marguerite asleep, taken through their own window. The message reads, 'You were always on the ledger.' The beat: terror made domestic—the case has been inside Marguerite's life all along.

chapters.title: Lena's Bargain
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena took the ledger to trade it back to Rowan for Marguerite's safety, believing Marguerite is the sister Rowan buried in 1987—kept alive under a new name, memory intact but sealed. The beat: Lena's loyalty revealed, and Marguerite's identity detonated.

chapters.title: The Name Not Yet Used
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite tests the impossible claim against their own past—adoption records, a scar, a lullaby only the bakery's radio ever played. The evidence holds. The beat: identity as the mystery's final cipher, and Marguerite as its last entry.

chapters.title: Going Live
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Rather than run, Marguerite plans the final podcast episode: reading the ledger on air, naming Rowan, forcing a town built on the swap to choose. Lena objects; the coroner's daughter offers corroboration. The beat: turning witness into weapon.

chapters.title: The Bakery at Closing Time
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Rowan—wearing Edith's face for thirty-five years—confronts Marguerite in the bakery before the broadcast. He offers the one thing Marguerite cannot price: the truth of the night their sister vanished, sealed forever if the ledger burns. The beat: temptation at its most intimate.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, climax. Marguerite goes live from the bakery itself, reads the ledger, and lets Rowan speak—his confession unfolding on air as he realizes the whole town is listening. Police, tipped by the coroner's daughter, arrive mid-sentence. The beat: exposure as both justice and self-annihilation.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Couldn't Hold
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Rowan is arrested; Lena is charged as accessory but cooperates. Marguerite recovers the burned fragment of the ledger's last page—their own original name, half-legible. The beat: victory with ash on it; some answers arrive already ruined.

chapters.title: Marguerite, or the Other Name
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Facing the choice to reclaim their buried identity or keep the one they built, Marguerite visits the sister's unmarked grave at last and speaks both names aloud. The beat: grief given a body; identity chosen, not assigned.

chapters.title: Cold Ledger, Warm Hands
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, resolution. The final episode airs with one entry withheld—Marguerite's own. Lena, out on bond, reopens the bakery under both women's names. Marguerite keeps the confession letter in a drawer, unanswered, and for the first time stops chasing the coldest case of all: themselves. The beat: belonging, finally, without proof.
